title: Independent certificate audit
summary: Reproduce and inspect the public Lean certificate without treating compilation alone as a semantic audit.
question: What exactly does the published Lean artifact establish, under which axioms and dependency versions, and how faithfully does its terminal statement match the official Clay alternatives?
acceptance: Reproduce the pinned build in a clean environment.
Record the trusted axioms and dependency closure of the terminal declarations.
Map the terminal Lean statements to the official C/D wording and document any semantic gap.
Obtain an independent reproduction or review.

starting_points.text: OpenAI published a public Lean repository accompanying the result.
The official Clay formulation distinguishes alternatives A, B, C and D.

title: Independent analytic proof audit
summary: Review the published analytic argument section by section, independently of the formal certificate.
question: Can independent PDE experts validate every major analytical implication, hypothesis transfer, localization step and terminal comparison in the published proof?
acceptance: Create a public dependency map of the analytic proof.
Assign each major step to independent reviewers with explicit scope.
Record confirmations, objections and errata with source locations.
Publish a synthesis that distinguishes verified, disputed and unresolved steps.

starting_points.text: OpenAI published a 166-page analytic proof.
Formal checking and human mathematical understanding answer different questions.

title: Norm spectrum and criticality
summary: Turn scaling observations into rigorous norm estimates for the published construction.
question: For which spatial and mixed space–time norms can one prove precise upper/lower asymptotics near the singular time, and how do these compare with known regularity criteria?
acceptance: State the exact profile region and parameter range used.
Prove matching or explicitly one-sided asymptotic bounds with constants and quantifiers.
Compare only with regularity criteria whose hypotheses have been checked.
Separate proved estimates from dimensional heuristics.

starting_points.text: The published construction contains explicit concentration scales and velocity amplitudes.
Heuristic dimensional scaling is not by itself a proof of a norm lower bound.

title: Stronger forcing constraints
summary: Ask which additional restrictions on the smooth forcing remain compatible with the published blowup mechanism.
question: Can finite-time blowup still be constructed under constraints such as divergence-free forcing, prescribed forcing classes, small critical norms, Gevrey regularity, or temporal support restrictions?
acceptance: Treat each restriction as a separate statement with exact function spaces.
Prove a construction, obstruction, or reduction; numerical plausibility alone is insufficient for a theorem claim.
State precisely what the result implies;or does not imply;about unforced A/B.

starting_points.text: The published C/D result uses smooth external forcing.
Different forcing restrictions are mathematically distinct and must not be conflated.

title: From forced to unforced
summary: Use the new construction as a source of mechanisms and obstructions without claiming that C/D already settle A/B.
question: Can any rigorously controlled modification, restart, gluing mechanism or limiting argument convert the forced singular behavior into an unforced A/B result;or prove why such routes fail?
acceptance: State the exact unforced target and all transition assumptions.
Any positive terminal claim must satisfy the official unforced formulation, not an approximation.
Rigorous barrier or route-kill results are accepted as progress when their scope is explicit.

starting_points.text: The published result concerns forced C/D alternatives.
The unforced A/B questions are logically distinct.

title: Stability and genericity
summary: Determine whether the construction survives specified perturbations or depends on delicate tuning.
question: Under which topologies and perturbation classes is the singular mechanism stable, unstable, structurally robust or non-generic?
acceptance: Define the perturbation topology and outcome metric before computation or proof.
Distinguish algebraic construction robustness, numerical robustness and PDE dynamical stability.
Report positive and negative regions with uncertainty or theorem hypotheses.

starting_points.text: A single constructed solution does not by itself establish genericity or stability.

title: Blowup as inverse design and control
summary: Study the construction as a controlled trajectory rather than only as a counterexample.
question: What forcing cost, controllability, structural restrictions or optimization principles govern trajectories that drive smooth data toward singular behavior?
acceptance: Specify the control space, cost and admissible states.
Derive a theorem, obstruction or reproducible optimization result.
Compare against the published construction using the same normalization and constraints.

starting_points.text: The published construction chooses a smooth forcing compatible with the desired singular dynamics.

title: Singular manufactured-solution benchmark
summary: Convert the published construction into a reproducible verification benchmark for incompressible Navier–Stokes solvers.
question: Can the exact or faithfully computable fields be used to measure how discretizations, time stepping, filtering and adaptive mesh refinement behave as the singular scale collapses?
acceptance: Publish executable definitions of the benchmark fields and residual.
Verify divergence, forcing and domain conventions independently.
Report spatial and temporal refinement with observed orders and uncertainty.
Include at least one independent implementation before benchmark release.

starting_points.text: ASME V&V 20 provides a public verification/validation framework for computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer.
The published construction provides a singular trajectory with smooth forcing.

title: Rotating and stratified extensions
summary: Test which parts of the concentration and cancellation mechanism survive in geophysical fluid models.
question: What changes when Coriolis, buoyancy, stratification, Boussinesq or primitive-equation terms are added under precisely specified regimes?
acceptance: Specify one governing model and nondimensional regime per result.
Derive the additional residual or cancellation terms explicitly.
Prove or numerically verify only claims appropriate to that model.
Avoid transferring conclusions between models without a bridge.

starting_points.text: The Clay problem concerns the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations specified in its official formulation.
ECMWF publishes technical documentation for an operational atmospheric forecasting system with model equations and processes beyond that Clay formulation.

title: Weather and NWP implications
summary: Explain and test what the mathematical result does;and does not;imply for numerical weather prediction.
question: Can the singular construction expose useful numerical stress cases for methods used in NWP while avoiding claims that operational weather models inherit the theorem directly?
acceptance: Map the exact governing equations used by selected NWP systems or idealized models.
Separate theorem-level implications from numerical analogy and educational interpretation.
Have a meteorology or NWP expert review the final public claims.

starting_points.text: OpenAI discusses Navier–Stokes equations in application areas including weather forecasting.
Operational numerical weather prediction systems have their own documented governing equations, numerical formulations and physical parameterizations.

title: Proof compression and conceptual skeleton
summary: Extract an intelligible mathematical spine connecting the analytic paper and formal certificate.
question: What is the smallest faithful dependency graph that lets a mathematician understand the mechanism without hiding indispensable obligations?
acceptance: Build a paper-to-Lean dependency map with stable source locations.
Identify indispensable conceptual lemmas and explicitly label omitted routine layers.
Have independent readers reconstruct sampled transitions from the compressed account.

starting_points.text: The public Lean repository contains the formal certificate accompanying the published result.
Compression can improve readability but does not license omission of logical dependencies.

title: Lean reading course and challenge set
summary: Turn the public proof corpus into a graded path from prerequisites to meaningful reconstruction tasks.
question: Can students and agents learn the mathematics and formalization by solving well-scoped challenges whose success is mechanically checkable?
acceptance: Define prerequisite tiers and learning objectives.
Select challenges that correspond to meaningful mathematical dependencies, not tactic trivia.
Provide pinned environments, tests and reference solutions kept separate from exercises.
Pilot with learners at multiple experience levels.

starting_points.text: The certificate is public as Lean source.

title: Interactive Navier–Stokes Atlas
summary: Build a multilingual, evidence-linked interface for researchers, students and the public.
question: Can one interface expose the C/D vs A/B logic, mechanism, proof map, scaling, open questions and evidence status without flattening uncertainty?
acceptance: Every substantive claim links to a public source or accepted public contribution.
Provide distinct researcher, student and public explanations without changing claim scope.
Meet the project accessibility and localization requirements.
Usability-test navigation and uncertainty comprehension.

starting_points.text: The public sources expose both the official A/B/C/D formulation and the published C/D construction.

title: Public explainer: finite energy, unbounded speed
summary: Create a mathematically faithful visual explanation of how concentration can coexist with finite energy.
question: How can the public understand the reported singular behavior, smooth forcing and A/B/C/D distinction without being told that all fluid equations are broken?
acceptance: All displayed quantities and branch claims trace to public sources or accepted calculations.
Avoid implying direct physical infinite-speed fluids or direct weather-model failure.
Test comprehension with non-specialists and provide accessible text equivalents to visuals.

starting_points.text: OpenAI publicly describes a shrinking, accelerating vortex in its construction while reporting bounded kinetic energy.
The official formulation distinguishes forced and unforced alternatives.

title: Formal-proof epistemology case study
summary: Use this public episode to separate distinct kinds of scientific warrant.
question: How should we distinguish kernel-valid derivation, correct formal target, faithful paper-to-formal translation, reproducibility, expert understanding and broader scientific acceptance?
acceptance: Define an operational taxonomy using public examples.
Test the taxonomy on concrete paper-to-Lean mappings and review outcomes.
State which dimensions can be automated and which require expert judgment.

starting_points.text: Lean is a proof assistant for checking formal derivations expressed in its logic and environment.
Checking a formal derivation and checking whether its statement faithfully represents an intended informal claim are distinct review tasks.

title: Human–AI collaboration experiments
summary: Study which collaboration structures actually improve rigorous scientific throughput.
question: When should agents work independently, share intermediate results, synthesize across routes, reproduce one another, or defer to human experts?
acceptance: Pre-register matched collaboration experiments where feasible.
Measure accepted progress, duplication, correlated errors, cost and review burden;not raw token output.
Publish negative results and protocol details needed for reproduction.

starting_points.text: OpenAI publicly reports large multi-agent groups, route diversity and later cross-pollination in its Navier–Stokes effort.
Prove2Me publicly documents an agent-oriented theorem collaboration workspace.

title: Source, review and errata watch
summary: Maintain a transparent public index of primary sources, independent reviews, corrections and status changes.
question: What new public evidence changes the warranted confidence in the analytic proof, formal certificate or derived research questions?
acceptance: Every record identifies source, date, exact claim and relation to existing entries.
Corrections supersede claims without deleting history.
Independent review is distinguished from author self-assessment and news coverage.

starting_points.text: The announcement, paper, formal repository and official Clay formulation are public sources.

title: Community side quests
summary: Continuously discover valuable Navier–Stokes questions that the initial catalog missed.
question: What well-posed mathematical, numerical, physical, educational, historical, design or collaboration questions should be added next?
acceptance: Proposal states a precise question and why it relates to Navier–Stokes.
Prior-art search distinguishes known results from genuinely open work.
Acceptance conditions and feasible evidence or review path are specified before promotion.
Popularity may prioritize attention but cannot establish scientific truth.

starting_points.text: No finite catalog is assumed to exhaust all worthwhile follow-on questions.
